claims.text: The starting alloy is equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% of each element.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance.
Pack-cementation aluminization will produce a nano-to-micrometer-thin surface layer.
Controlled surface aluminization will form a continuous, adherent Al2O3 barrier on cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The Al2O3 surface layer will impede oxygen ingress during high-temperature exposure.
Impeded oxygen ingress will reduce internal oxidation of HfNbTaTiZr.
The aluminization treatment and subsequent exposure will leave the cast bulk microstructure unchanged.
Preserving the cast bulk microstructure will preserve the alloy's ductility and yield strength.
After 100 hours in air at 1000 °C, aluminized HfNbTaTiZr will have lower oxidation mass gain than untreated material.
After 100 hours in air at 1000 °C, aluminized HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit less oxygen penetration than untreated material.
The aluminized alloy will retain 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility after the specified exposure.
The aluminized alloy will retain a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C under strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1 after the specified exposure.
The proposed benefit is bounded to oxidizing conditions near 1000 °C and exposure durations of approximately 100 hours.
